name: talisman-efcb1a36-blind30-ots
instr:
# Repairing a Go secret-guarding command-line tool without a test suite

This is a command-line guard a developer hooks into a repository to stop secrets being committed, pushed or carried in history, and it now gives the wrong answer in a great many places. Nothing about the repositories it inspects changed and nothing about how it is invoked changed. Secrets it used to catch now slip through, a few innocent things are now objected to, and several runs end with the opposite exit status to the one they earn. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything we could observe from the outside.

Hooking it in ahead of a push and feeding it the four whitespace-separated values a push supplies on standard input — a local branch name, a local hash, a remote branch name, a remote hash — then asking it back for the old and new commit hashes gives the wrong fields: what comes back as the old hash is a branch name rather than the hash that followed it, and the new one is shifted the same way.

Asking what a staged change adds is wrong too. With one modified file and one newly created file staged, the text attributed to each new or changed file no longer equals the file on disk: the captured bytes carry the diff's own header lines with them, and a staged file inside a folder whose name contains a space comes back the same way.
